title: asymmetric-nvlink-handshake-lab-notes-2028-04-17
content:
Summary:

Short version: observed a recurring ~5–10 minute window where NVLink peer-training fails asymmetrically between two slots on the same chassis. Symptoms: transient correctable ECC spikes (soft errors), partial link up state on one side, and occasional driver watchdogs that result in process-level GPU hangs (no full node panic). This doc collects small-night-lab reproduction attempts, raw ergonomics, telemetry snippets, and next hypothesis steps.

Why this matters:
- Causes intermittent degraded throughput on multi-GPU model shards (increasing tail latency)
- Triggers worker evictions when driver watchdogs escalate to process aborts
- Hard to catch because it often self-recovers and leaves minimal dmesg artifacts

Observed pattern (recurring over last three weeks):
- Weekdays 01:10–03:00 UTC: increased incidence of job retries flagged with "peer link degraded" and "cuda kernel timeout"
- Each incident cluster shows a short-lived ECC correctable error surge on GPU-A (slot 3) while GPU-B (slot 4) shows link training warnings on its nvlink logs
- Often follows a firmware update to one node in the rack or an upstream switch microcode bump

Key telemetry excerpts (sanitized):
- nvidia-smi topo -m around incident:
  GPU0 GPU1 GPU2 GPU3
  GPU0   X    NV4  NV1  NV1
  ...
- dmesg snippets pulled within 2 minutes of event:
  [  903.412345] NVRM: GPU 0000:3a:00: GPU has fallen off the bus.
  [  903.412379] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:3a:00): 13, PID=27431, ... \n  [  904.123456] nvlink0: link-training: lane 2 failed to sync (peer reports asymmetric coefficients)
  [  904.123460] nvlink0: link-state: side-A=UP side-B=TRAINING

- telemetry (aggregated counters):
  ECC_correctable_count spike: +540 in 120s window on slot 3
  nvlink_train_failures: 3 in same window
  driver_watchdog_count: 1 (process terminated, no kernel panic)

Lab repro attempts run on isolated bench chassis (intel server w/ 4x H100-SKU-XYZ, mixed firmware):
- Config matrix run (short):
  A: both GPUs firmware v1.2.0 (baseline) -> no repro in 2h window
  B: GPU-A v1.2.0, GPU-B v1.3.1 -> reproduced 2/5 trials (link training failure within 15–40m)
  C: both v1.3.1 -> less frequent but still observed once in 3h
  D: same FW but NVSwitch microcode mismatch (old switch fw) -> immediate deterministic repro in bench within 5m

Steps used for bench repro (commands and notes):
- Start continuous memory-copy stress: cuda-memtest variant with 8GB contiguous allocations and 8 worker threads per GPU
- Simulate background cross-GPU traffic: small allreduce loop using NCCL (fp16) at 200MB/s sustained
- Watch dmesg tail + nvlink logs:
  sudo journalctl -f -u nvlink-monitor.service &
  while true; do dmesg --ctime | tail -n 40 >> /tmp/runlog.txt; sleep 3; done &

Quick actionable findings so far:
- Mixed firmware across peers dramatically increases probability of asymmetric handshake failures. Exact cutoff appears around v1.2.x <-> v1.3.x in our bench hardware (H100 variants).
- NVSwitch microcode mismatch is strongly correlated and can be a reliable repro vector in lab
- ECC count spikes appear shortly after training failure — suggests transient link-level noise rather than long-term memory wear
- Driver watchdogs are secondary: link training failure -> increased error retries -> kernel watchdog trips on long-running kernels

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Training coefficient negotiation protocol changed between firmware families; older side sends coefficients that newer side rejects -> asymmetric state
2) Switch microcode enforces stricter CRC/handshake timeouts causing one-sided tear-downs
3) Thermal or power transient amplifies bit errors during retraining window (less likely given isolated bench reproducibility)

Open questions / unknowns:
- Why do some mixed FW combos not reproduce? (likely minor patch differences, need exact build ids)
- Is there a hidden backoff / retry timer divergence between stacks that leaves one side in TRAINING indefinitely?
- Does the kernel driver coalesce/link-state across multiple NVLink ports and hide per-lane failures?

Next experiments to run (short list):
- Collect full firmware and microcode hashes from failing nodes (nvlink-fwtool dump) and attach to JIRA-SRE-2147.
- Add fine-grain telemetry: sample NVLink lane CRC counters every 2s during stress. Ingest into bench TSDB for correlation.
- Re-run bench with isolated power droop emulation (software-controlled PSU emulation) to rule out power transient hypothesis.
- Test with patched driver that increases handshake verbosity (build local debug kernel module) and capture transaction-level logs.

Operational mitigations (short-term):
- For critical fleets, prefer homogeneous firmware rollouts; enforce pre-rollout bench checks that include NVLink training step.
- Add a short-lived circuit-breaker: if nvlink_train_failures > 5 within 5m, gracefully migrate shards off the node before driver watchdog escalates.
- Update onboarding runbook to explicitly check NVSwitch microcode version during node provisioning.

Notes to self / oncall handover for next night shift:
- If you see "link-state: side-A=UP side-B=TRAINING" in dmesg, do not reboot immediately. Collect the following first:
  1) nvlink-fwtool dump -> /tmp/nvlink-dump-$(date +%s).txt
  2) nvidia-smi --query-gpu=gpu_name,firmware --format=csv
  3) copy /var/log/journal entries between -5m and +2m window
- If driver watchdog kills a process but node remains responsive, escalate to "eviction-prep" (move running shards) rather than full node reset.

Draft action items (owners):
- Diego: automate nvlink-fwtool collection in our incident capture job (deadline: 2028-04-24)
- Priya: add NVSwitch microcode check to provisioning pipeline (WIP, PR #432)
- Ethan: prototype fine-grain CRC telemetry ingestion to bench TSDB (POC by 2028-05-01)
- Maya (me): attempt debug build driver with handshake logging and coordinate oncall capture window (2028-04-20 night run)

Appendix: quick copy-paste useful commands
- nvidia-smi -q -d ECC,LINK
- sudo nvlink-fwtool dump > /tmp/nvlink-$(hostname)-$(date +%s).txt
- grep -i "nvlink" /var/log/kern.log | tail -n 200
- python3 tools/telemetry/extract_counts.py --start -00:05:00 --end +00:02:00 --counters nvlink_crc,ecc_correctable

Rough log snippet (for evidence upload):
[2028-04-17 01:22:14] nvlink0: lane-2-CRC: 12 -> 476 (12s)
[2028-04-17 01:22:15] nvlink0: link-training: negotiation timeout (side-B)
[2028-04-17 01:22:20] ECC: GPU 0000:3a:00 correctable count +180
[2028-04-17 01:22:46] NVRM: Xid 43: GPU watchdog timeout (pid=7821)

Concluding notes:
This is a working log, intentionally rough. The mix of firmware/microcode appears central; the path to mitigation likely lies in either enforced homogeneous rollouts or driver/switch patches that gracefully handle coefficient mismatches. Next immediate win is automating artifact capture so oncall can escalate with high-fidelity dumps rather than best-effort notes.

-- Maya
